This one is about running lighter and about a lot of new things to point a camera at. Telescope uses much less graphics memory and processor, the downloads shrank, and there are new tools for the night sky, photos and building a picture out of several streams.

## Lighter and faster

- Graphics memory went from 292 MB to about 140 MB idle and from 379 MB to 223 MB at 1080p.
- The desktop program is 15 MB smaller, the Linux download about 13 MB smaller and the phone app went from 7.1 MB to 2.1 MB.
- A plain 4K stream into a 1080p camera takes about a quarter of the processor it did (22% of a core down to 6%), and on Windows about a third.
- Background blur at 4K went from 49% of a core to 16% while holding 30 fps, and Auto framing at 4K from about 100% to 57%.
- With Power-saving effects on, Auto framing at Head or Chest follows your face and uses about a third of the processor it did.
- The Windows 11 camera shows each picture about 17 ms sooner. A phone that sends 24 fps now shows its own 24 fps.
- With hardware decoding on Linux a plain 4K stream went from 41% of a core to 28%.
- The app wakes far less often while it sits in the tray.
- Intel graphics on Windows no longer slowly eat memory during a long stream (it was about 10 MB a minute).

## Slow computers

When frames start running late, Telescope now runs heavy effects less often and returns to full rate once there's room. In battery saver it starts at the **Power-saving** level. An **Adjusting** chip in the top bar lists every change with buttons to undo it for this run or switch it off, and **Automatic adjustments** under Video in Settings has a switch for each. More in `docs/features/app.md`.

## New

- **Stargazer** (Lab). Lucky imaging, live stacking and star trails from video or photos, and a Night shot with long exposures. See `docs/features/effects.md`.
- **Phototrap** (Lab). Takes a burst of photos when something moves in a zone you drew.
- **Merge bracket** on the Photos card turns a focus or exposure bracket into one picture. Brackets got more dials, the shutter list runs from 1/4000 s, and photos follow Transforms (mirror, rotation, a **Use zoom** crop).
- **One picture** is a proper scene editor now. Exact position and size fields, a layer list with an eye, a lock and drag to reorder, transitions between layouts (Glide, Shuffle, Crossfade and some sillier ones), an **Auto director** that switches layout when your hands show up for another stream, and a **Cut out** switch to show only the person in a tile.
- **Spout send** (Lab) shares a stream's finished picture with OBS or another program on the same computer. A Spout sender on Windows, a PipeWire video source on Linux.
- **Headset** on the 3D card shows the picture in a Quest's browser, one half per eye, and the headset needs no app.
- Nikon and Canon DSLRs work on Windows too, with live view, photos, focus and exposure. Canon there is less tested, since I only had a Nikon to try them with.
- **Look** in Settings has options for corners, text size, density, contrast, motion and tooltip delay.
- A graphics card choice in Settings, for when the system picks the wrong one.
- Paired phones find the computer again after a Wi-Fi change without pairing again.
- The Windows setup offers **Install for all users** and a folder choice.
- MCP can change the settings of most plugins now, and presets save a lot more (Composite zoom, USB webcam, microphone, Photos, Phototrap and Stargazer).
- A plugin that crashes is switched off for the run and the rest of the app carries on.

## Changed

- Telescope's ports moved to 7479 to 7482 (they were 8765 to 8768) and presence uses UDP 7483. Rules you added yourself in a firewall or Tailscale need the new ports.
- **Go back to the Python version** button in Settings is gone. Updating from the Python app still works.
- The first Exposure choice on the Photos card reads **Video**.

## Fixed

- **Local only** could leave the stream reachable over Wi-Fi while the switch said USB only.
- Blur now and Chroma key no longer flash a dark frame.
- The first frames an app gets from the Windows 11 camera show the last picture and not black.
- A photo that can't be turned or cropped is saved untouched.
- Pairing over a USB cable no longer ends in a "Pairing failed" dialog right after "Paired".
- Updates that were cut short can't leave Windows or Linux without a working Telescope any more.
